indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of chronic
an ache is a dull, lasting pain

explanation.surface: Someone tries to conceal where their long-term pain comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store, and as a noun it means a hiding place for valuables or supplies.

clue.text: Vegetable initially cooked very much al dente

indicators.note: initially points to the beginning of the following word, so only its opening letter counts

parts.note: the first letter of cooked
al dente pasta is firm to the bite; taken further it is simply hard

explanation.surface: A cook's greens have been left far too firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy green garden vegetable related to beet, eaten as a cooked leaf.

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over and throw its parts into disorder

parts.note: all eight letters of these words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A heckler boos to rattle a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A choirboy is a young male member of a church choir, so he is one kind of vocalist.

indicators.note: something running is in motion and unsettled, so its letters move into a new order

parts.note: the six letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child tries to grab a mum or dad who is jogging past.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to trick or snare someone, which is a way of capturing them, as a verb.

indicators.note: holding means wrapping round, so the word for mother encloses the next piece

parts.note: mater is Latin for mother, used in old-fashioned British slang
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: At cards, Mum is holding spades, and the question is whether she has the ace.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is an expert, someone with complete skill at a craft, the same as a master of it.

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a flag is a type of iris, the plant with sword-shaped leaves

explanation.surface: An instruction to highlight a voice assistant for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag reads as a verb, mark for attention, but here it is the waterside plant, the yellow flag iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Siri is Apple's voice-controlled helper on phones, a software assistant that answers spoken requests.

definitions.note: used adjectivally: of the same family

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: someone visibly embarrassed blushes, going red in the face
late can mean former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: Someone blushes when talking about their ex-family.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are kin share a bloodline, so being of one family means being connected by birth or marriage.

clue.text: Fruit, a number outside crate, damaged

indicators.note: damaged goods are knocked out of shape, so the letters of the crate get rearranged
outside means lying around something else, so the number wraps the other piece

parts.note: nine is one number among many
these letters are rearranged before going inside

explanation.surface: A greengrocer finds fruit sitting outside a broken box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' could be any figure; it has to be one long enough to split around five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a common stone fruit.

parts.note: curt means short or abrupt in manner
an ailment is a minor illness

explanation.surface: A short bout of sickness cut someone's time down.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to cut short, so the noun names a reduction in length or duration.

clue.text: Take on work in audit regularly

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the letters that follow
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of audit
OP is short for opus, Latin for a work

explanation.surface: An accountant takes on extra work during an audit.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt is to take something up as your own, such as a policy or a child, to accept it.

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are tipped out and come out in a new order

parts.note: the seven letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wine that went off and became even worse to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine with a distinctive resin taste added from pine sap.

indicators.note: to see something partially is to see only a part of it, so look within the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A nature-watcher glimpses a praying mantis lying still.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is inactive or asleep for a while, the way animals hibernate through winter.

clue.text: KLM maybe fine with hours lost

indicators.note: lost means gone missing, so the abbreviation is removed

parts.note: a hairline crack or margin is a very fine one
H is the standard abbreviation for hours

explanation.surface: A traveller says the Dutch carrier is fine apart from the time it wastes.
explanation.walkthrough: KLM is the Dutch national airline; 'maybe' marks it as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: KLM is an example of a company that runs scheduled passenger flights.

clue.text: Water equipment limited by one speed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: limited by means bounded on each side, so one word sits enclosed inside another

parts.note: rate is a measure of speed
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Kit for watering that can only run at a single speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' looks like a noun in the surface, but the definition is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate is to supply land with water through channels or pipes so crops grow.

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent
tone is the quality of a sound or colour

explanation.surface: An advert praises a top-grade cleaning fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a colourless liquid used to dissolve other substances, as in nail-varnish remover.

clue.text: Clear glass of claret's drunk (last of day for English)

indicators.note: something drunk staggers about out of order, so the letters are jumbled
putting one thing for another means swapping it in as a replacement

parts.note: the word with its S, before any change

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the next word only

parts.note: the final letter of day
E is the abbreviation for English; this letter leaves

explanation.surface: A clear wine glass of red has been drained, the last of the day's drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap E out of CLARETS for Y to get CLARTSY, then rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal is high-quality transparent glass, the kind used for fine wine glasses and decanters.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tiny quantity, as in a little bit
second meaning: a British layered dessert of sponge, fruit, custard and cream

explanation.surface: Asking for just a little dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, pudding means dessert in general.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a tiny portion of something and a cold dessert of sponge, jelly, custard and cream.

parts.note: something in is fashionable
a deed is an act or action

explanation.surface: A performer's turn is really well liked.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an adverb affirming something as certainly or really so, used for emphasis.

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for minutes
an ending is the finishing of something

explanation.surface: A repair job takes only minutes to complete.
explanation.walkthrough: Finishing off looks like an instruction to take a last letter, but it is simply a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Mending is the work of fixing broken things, so as a noun it covers a repair job.

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a reed is a tall grass growing in wet places

explanation.surface: A moralising claim that smoking good weed is sinful.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice, one of the seven deadly vices in Christian teaching, is excessive desire for wealth.

indicators.note: soundly here means going by sound, so the words are judged as spoken

parts.note: to tack is to fix with small nails
a tile is a thin slab for covering roofs

explanation.surface: A roofer firmly secures a slab, hands on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile describes things relating to the sense of touch, or a person who likes physical contact.

clue.text: Aromatic spice but left out bay

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for left is taken away

parts.note: a clove is a dried flower bud used as a spice
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A cook skipped a fragrant spice but added a leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Bay looks like the cooking leaf beside the spice, but it is a stretch of coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A cove is a small sheltered inlet on a coastline, a little curved stretch of water.

clue.text: Get rid of king with moderate protection

indicators.note: protection wraps round what it guards, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to ease is to moderate or lessen
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Overthrow a monarch who has only light security.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or delete completely, removing all trace of something.

clue.text: Book short month with European renter mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: NOV is the calendar abbreviation for November
E is the abbreviation for European
a letter is one who lets property; here someone who rents it out

explanation.surface: A short book bought in some month from a European landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short month' looks like it shortens the month, but short belongs to the definition: a book that is short.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a brief novel or long short story, a shorter work of fiction.

clue.text: Fear of departed around end of October?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for departed wraps the other letter

parts.note: the departed are those who have died

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of October

explanation.surface: Fear of ghosts when Halloween comes at the close of October.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great apprehension or terror about something to come, a noun close to anxiety.
